<div class="page-shell">

<header class="masthead">
  <div class="eyebrow">WebR practical</div>
  <h1>Odds, log-odds, and odds ratios</h1>
  <p>Move between the scales, inspect exponentiated R output, and practise the language used in papers.</p>
</header>

<section class="panel">

<h2>Overview</h2>

This practical follows the introduction to logistic regression and the coefficient-interpretation lesson. You will:

<ul class="tight-list">
  <li>convert between probability, odds, and log-odds;</li>
  <li>distinguish an odds value from an odds ratio;</li>
  <li>turn a log-odds coefficient into an odds ratio with <code>exp()</code>;</li>
  <li>use <code>broom::tidy(..., exponentiate = TRUE)</code>;</li>
  <li>interpret odds ratios in R output, tables, and paper-style sentences.</li>
</ul>

<div class="scale-grid">
  <div class="scale-card"><strong>Probability</strong><span>One chance, from 0 to 1</span></div>
  <div class="scale-card"><strong>Odds</strong><span>One chance, from 0 to infinity</span></div>
  <div class="scale-card"><strong>Log-odds</strong><span>One chance, from minus to plus infinity</span></div>
  <div class="scale-card compare"><strong>Odds ratio</strong><span>A comparison of two odds</span></div>
</div>

</section>

<section class="panel">

<h2>Part 1. Probability and odds</h2>

If the event probability is $p$, the probability that it does not happen is $1-p$. Odds compare these two quantities.

<div class="formula-panel">
$$
\text{odds}=\frac{p}{1-p}
\qquad\qquad
p=\frac{\text{odds}}{1+\text{odds}}
$$
</div>

For example, $p=0.75$ gives odds of $0.75/0.25=3$. The event has odds of 3 to 1.

</section>

<div class="webr-wrap">

<h3>R code: convert probabilities to odds</h3>

Run the code, then change the probabilities and run it again.

```{webr-r}
p <- c(0.10, 0.25, 0.50, 0.75, 0.90)
odds <- p / (1 - p)
data.frame(probability = p, odds = round(odds, 3))
```

</div>

<div class="practice" data-answer="b">
  <div class="practice-title">Question 1</div>
  <p>An event has probability 0.20. What are its odds?</p>
  <div class="choice-set">
    <label><input type="radio" name="p1" value="a">0.20, because odds and probability are the same.</label>
    <label><input type="radio" name="p1" value="b">0.25, because <code>0.20 / 0.80 = 0.25</code>.</label>
  </div>
  <button type="button">Check</button>
  <div class="practice-feedback" data-correct="Correct. Odds compare the event probability with the probability of no event." data-incorrect="Not quite. Divide 0.20 by 1 minus 0.20, which gives 0.25."></div>
</div>

<div class="practice" data-answer="a">
  <div class="practice-title">Question 2</div>
  <p>What do odds of 3 mean?</p>
  <div class="choice-set">
    <label><input type="radio" name="p2" value="a">The event is three times as likely to happen as not to happen.</label>
    <label><input type="radio" name="p2" value="b">The probability of the event is 3.</label>
  </div>
  <button type="button">Check</button>
  <div class="practice-feedback" data-correct="Correct. Odds compare happens with does not happen. Probabilities cannot exceed 1." data-incorrect="Not quite. Odds can exceed 1, but probability cannot. Odds of 3 means 3 to 1."></div>
</div>

<section class="panel">

<h2>Part 2. Odds and log-odds</h2>

Logistic regression models the natural log of the odds. This quantity is also called the logit.

<div class="formula-panel">
$$
\text{log-odds}=\ln(\text{odds})=\ln\!\left(\frac{p}{1-p}\right)
$$
</div>

<ul class="tight-list">
  <li>Odds below 1 have negative log-odds.</li>
  <li>Odds of 1 have log-odds of 0 and probability 0.50.</li>
  <li>Odds above 1 have positive log-odds.</li>
</ul>

The inverse operation is exponentiation: <code>exp(log_odds)</code> returns odds.

<div class="arrow-chain">probability <span>→</span> odds <span>→</span> log-odds</div>

</section>

<div class="webr-wrap">

<h3>R code: move across all three scales</h3>

```{webr-r}
p <- c(0.20, 0.50, 0.80)
odds <- p / (1 - p)
log_odds <- log(odds)

data.frame(
  probability = p,
  odds = round(odds, 3),
  log_odds = round(log_odds, 3),
  back_to_odds = round(exp(log_odds), 3)
)
```

</div>

<div class="practice" data-answer="b">
  <div class="practice-title">Question 3</div>
  <p>An event has log-odds of <code>-1.10</code>. What can you say without doing a precise calculation?</p>
  <div class="choice-set">
    <label><input type="radio" name="p3" value="a">Its probability is above 0.50.</label>
    <label><input type="radio" name="p3" value="b">Its probability is below 0.50.</label>
  </div>
  <button type="button">Check</button>
  <div class="practice-feedback" data-correct="Correct. Negative log-odds correspond to odds below 1 and probability below 0.50." data-incorrect="Not quite. Negative log-odds mean odds below 1, so the event is less likely than not."></div>
</div>

<section class="panel">

<h2>Part 3. From a coefficient to an odds ratio</h2>

In the weak-grip model, the age coefficient is 0.1168. It is the change in log-odds for a one-year increase in age.

<div class="formula-panel">
$$
\text{log-odds of weak grip}=-8.824+0.1168\times\text{age}
$$
$$
\text{odds ratio per year}=e^{0.1168}=1.124
$$
</div>

The coefficient is additive on the log-odds scale. The odds ratio is multiplicative on the odds scale.

<div class="report"><strong>Interpretation:</strong> Each additional year of age is associated with 1.124 times the odds, or 12.4% higher odds, of weak grip.</div>

This is not a 12.4 percentage-point increase in probability.

</section>

<div class="webr-wrap">

<h3>R code: exponentiate coefficients</h3>

Complete the blanks with the age coefficient, then try 5-year and 10-year intervals.

```{webr-r}
age_coefficient <- ____

exp(age_coefficient)       # one-year odds ratio
exp(5 * age_coefficient)   # five-year odds ratio
exp(10 * age_coefficient)  # ten-year odds ratio
```

</div>

<details class="answer">
<summary>Show the answer and possible output</summary>

```r
age_coefficient <- 0.1168
exp(age_coefficient)
exp(5 * age_coefficient)
exp(10 * age_coefficient)
```

```text
[1] 1.123932
[1] 1.793197
[1] 3.215993
```

</details>

<div class="practice" data-answer="b">

  <div class="choice-set">

<section class="panel">

<h2>Part 4. Exponentiated output from broom</h2>

Run the setup cell first. It reads the same KLOSA data used in the logistic-regression lessons and fits the age model.

</section>

<div class="webr-wrap">

<h3>R code: fit the model</h3>

```{webr-r}
klosa <- read.csv(
  "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/the-graph-courses/rsr_resources/refs/heads/main/data/28_klosa_men_grip.csv"
)

grip_model <- glm(
  weak_grip ~ age,
  family = binomial,
  data = klosa
)

coef(grip_model)
```

</div>

<div class="webr-wrap">

<h3>R code: request odds ratios and confidence intervals</h3>

Fill in <code>TRUE</code> for both arguments.

```{webr-r}
broom::tidy(
  grip_model,
  exponentiate = ____,
  conf.int = ____
)
```

</div>

<details class="answer">
<summary>Show the completed code and possible output</summary>

```r
broom::tidy(
  grip_model,
  exponentiate = TRUE,
  conf.int = TRUE
)
```

```text
# A tibble: 2 x 7
  term        estimate std.error statistic p.value conf.low conf.high
  <chr>          <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>   <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl>
1 (Intercept) 0.000147    0.319      -27.6  <2e-16 0.0000783  0.000273
2 age         1.124       0.00476      24.6 <2e-16 1.114      1.135
```

</details>

<div class="callout warning">
<p>With <code>exponentiate = TRUE</code>, read <code>estimate</code>, <code>conf.low</code>, and <code>conf.high</code> on the odds-ratio scale. The standard error is not an odds ratio.</p>
</div>

<section class="panel">

<h2>Part 5. How papers present odds ratios</h2>

The same result may appear in a regression table:

<table class="paper-table">
  <thead><tr><th>Predictor</th><th>OR</th><th>95% CI</th><th>p</th></tr></thead>
  <tbody><tr><td>Age, per year</td><td>1.12</td><td>1.11 to 1.13</td><td>&lt;0.001</td></tr></tbody>
</table>

Or in a sentence:

<div class="report">Each additional year of age was associated with 12% higher odds of weak grip (OR 1.12, 95% CI 1.11 to 1.13, p &lt; 0.001).</div>

Good reporting names the outcome, states the comparison or unit, gives the odds ratio, and reports uncertainty.

</section>

<div class="practice" data-answer="b">
  <div class="practice-title">Question 8</div>
  <p>A paper reports <strong>OR 0.80, 95% CI 0.62 to 1.03</strong>. Which reading is best?</p>
  <div class="choice-set">
    <label><input type="radio" name="p8" value="a">The predictor definitely reduces the probability of the outcome by 20%.</label>
    <label><input type="radio" name="p8" value="b">The estimate suggests 20% lower odds, but the interval includes 1 and is compatible with no difference at the 5% level.</label>
  </div>
  <button type="button">Check</button>
  <div class="practice-feedback" data-correct="Correct. One is the no-difference value for an odds ratio, and this interval crosses 1." data-incorrect="Not quite. Check whether the 95% confidence interval includes the no-difference value of 1."></div>
</div>

<div class="practice" data-answer="a">
  <div class="practice-title">Question 9</div>
  <p>A paper says, “OR 2.0 for current smoking.” What information is needed to interpret the result precisely?</p>
  <div class="choice-set">
    <label><input type="radio" name="p9" value="a">The outcome and the smoking reference group, plus the confidence interval.</label>
    <label><input type="radio" name="p9" value="b">Nothing else. OR 2.0 always means a 100 percentage-point increase in probability.</label>
  </div>
  <button type="button">Check</button>
  <div class="practice-feedback" data-correct="Correct. An odds ratio needs a named outcome and comparison. The confidence interval communicates uncertainty." data-incorrect="Not quite. An odds ratio does not give a fixed probability change, and its comparison must be identified."></div>
</div>

<section class="panel">

<h2>Part 6. Categorical predictors and reference groups</h2>

For a categorical predictor, each odds ratio compares one displayed level with an omitted reference level.

```text
term             estimate conf.low conf.high
(Intercept)        0.0958   0.0834    0.110
age_group65-74     5.22     4.35      6.28
age_group75+      14.4     11.5      18.3
```

Here the reference group is men aged 45 to 64.

<div class="report">Compared with men aged 45 to 64, men aged 75 and above had 14.4 times the odds of weak grip (95% CI 11.5 to 18.3).</div>

</section>

<div class="webr-wrap">

<h3>R code: fit a categorical age model</h3>

Run this after the setup cell in Part 4.

```{webr-r}
klosa$age_group <- cut(
  klosa$age,
  breaks = c(45, 65, 75, Inf),
  right = FALSE,
  labels = c("45-64", "65-74", "75+")
)

group_model <- glm(
  weak_grip ~ age_group,
  family = binomial,
  data = klosa
)

broom::tidy(group_model, exponentiate = TRUE, conf.int = TRUE)
```

</div>

<div class="practice" data-answer="a">
  <div class="practice-title">Question 10</div>
  <p>What does the odds ratio 5.22 for <code>age_group65-74</code> compare?</p>
  <div class="choice-set">
    <label><input type="radio" name="p10" value="a">Men aged 65 to 74 with the reference group, men aged 45 to 64.</label>
    <label><input type="radio" name="p10" value="b">Men aged 65 to 74 with men aged 75 and above.</label>
  </div>
  <button type="button">Check</button>
  <div class="practice-feedback" data-correct="Correct. Every displayed category is compared with the omitted reference category." data-incorrect="Not quite. The omitted first factor level, 45 to 64, is the reference group."></div>
</div>

<script>
const COMPLETION_CODE = "ODDSRATIO";
const COMPLETION_REQUIRED = 8;

function updateCompletion() {
  const cards = document.querySelectorAll(".practice");
  const correct = document.querySelectorAll(".practice.is-correct").length;
  const total = cards.length;
  const progress = document.getElementById("code-progress");
  const box = document.getElementById("code-box");
  const value = document.getElementById("code-value");

  if (progress) {
    progress.textContent = correct + " of " + total + " correct (need at least " + COMPLETION_REQUIRED + ")";
  }

  if (box && value) {
    if (correct >= COMPLETION_REQUIRED) {
      value.textContent = COMPLETION_CODE;
      box.style.display = "block";
    } else {
      box.style.display = "none";
    }
  }
}

document.querySelectorAll(".practice").forEach((card) => {
  const button = card.querySelector("button");
  const feedback = card.querySelector(".practice-feedback");
  const answer = card.dataset.answer;

  button.addEventListener("click", () => {
    const selected = card.querySelector("input[type='radio']:checked");
    card.classList.remove("is-correct", "is-incorrect");
    card.querySelectorAll("label").forEach((label) => {
      label.classList.remove("correct-choice", "incorrect-choice");
    });

    if (!selected) {
      card.classList.add("is-incorrect");
      feedback.textContent = "Choose an answer first, then check it.";
      updateCompletion();
      return;
    }

    const selectedLabel = selected.closest("label");
    const correctInput = card.querySelector(`input[value="${answer}"]`);
    const correctLabel = correctInput ? correctInput.closest("label") : null;

    if (selected.value === answer) {
      card.classList.add("is-correct");
      selectedLabel.classList.add("correct-choice");
      feedback.textContent = feedback.dataset.correct;
    } else {
      card.classList.add("is-incorrect");
      selectedLabel.classList.add("incorrect-choice");
      if (correctLabel) correctLabel.classList.add("correct-choice");
      feedback.textContent = feedback.dataset.incorrect;
    }

    updateCompletion();
  });
});

updateCompletion();
</script>
